newsitem.title: USA: Marathon sees Ill. refinery work done in May.
newsitem.headline: Marathon sees Ill. refinery work done in May.

text.p: Marathon Oil Co, which early reported first quarter results, said it should complete the maintenance work now going on at its Robinson, Illinois refinery by early May.

"Turnaround activity is currently underway at Marathon's Robinson refinery and is planned to be completed in early May," the company said in written a statement accompanying its first quarter earnings report.
Oil traders have been saying in recent weeks that Marathon was planning extensive work on different units at the refinery, which can process 166,000 barrels of crude oil.
The company also said it completed, as scheduled, the planned maintenance at its 70,000 barrel per day refinery in Texas City, Texas during the first quarter.

Earlier the company reported first quarter operating results of $180 million or $0.62 cents a share on revenues of $4.08 billion versus $112 million or $0.39 a share on revenues of $3.63 billion in the 1996 first quarter.

"Led by strong upstream prices and improved downstream margins, Marathon's first quarter operating income improved substantially over 1996," USX Corp Chairman Thomas Usher said in the prepared statement.

Those income figures exclude a non-cash charge of $114 million in the 1997 quarter and a non-cash credit of $155 million related to the 1982 deal that made Marathon part of USX. Marathon Oil is a unit of USX-Marathon Group.
Including those items, the company's first quarter income per fully-diluted share amounted to $0.37 versus $0.74.
